commit_date_definition: Commit dates use Git committer timestamps (%cI), including their stored timezone offsets. Author metadata is retained separately; a rebase preserves authorship but creates a new committer/date.

upgrade_plan.title: Plan: upgrade to v2.0.0-jq.1
upgrade_plan.status: Proposed production flow; local rebase and rehearsal complete; production steps not executed
upgrade_plan.summary: Prepare and validate the release before the window. During maintenance, drain traffic, stop every old writer, take a coherent full backup, start one 2.0 instance to migrate, and verify it before reopening traffic. Keep a tested restore path through the observation period.
upgrade_plan.topology: The deployment repository documents the current internal environment as one host with Compose project bifrost-gateway, PostgreSQL 16, Nginx, Bifrost and Portal. Confirm the actual inventory and running state before scheduling. Use this maintenance cutover for that environment; a move to HA is a separate change.
decisions: Name the release maintainer, deployment owner and database/recovery owner; one person may fill several roles. Record who can decide to restore, the change window and the user notification channel.

Record the actual old source/image digests, database endpoints and sizes, storage engines, Compose files/overlays, mounts, background writers, encryption mode and key fingerprints. If production differs from the rehearsed jq.8/PostgreSQL/S3 setup, extend the rehearsal first.

Set maximum acceptable outage and data loss (RTO/RPO), plus a last safe rollback-start time based on measured restore and old-service verification time. The local 1.03-second pause is not a production downtime estimate.

Choose the immutable registry artifact and publication owner, backup destination/retention, recovery host and available disk space. Confirm old and new images can be pulled on the target architecture.

Agree on baseline request success, latency, stream completion, log delay and billing checks; define the observation window and rollback thresholds. A suggested starting point is 15 minutes of restricted traffic and 24 hours of close observation, adjusted to normal traffic volume and operational needs.

phases.title: Finish source review and freeze the release
phases.status: Local rebase done; shared review and release freeze pending
actions: Use feature/upstream-v2.0.0-rebase on exact transports/v2.0.0 (e4a30d604). Review the 21-commit ledger: 16 replayed, five omitted, plus billing integration and the OpenRouter reasoning fix. Preserve the jq.8 backup branch.

Refresh the internal-main comparison before release and account for any patches added since the rehearsal. Resolve conflicts by behavior and retain the documented tests; do not repeat the rebase if the reviewed source is still current.

Submit the source and report through the internal GitLab review/MR path to protected main. Record the accepted release SHA and ensure its runtime source matches verified implementation 8654f269a, apart from documentation. Any runtime change needs relevant tests and a new verified artifact.
phases.gate: Every internal patch is accounted for; the reviewed release SHA and test evidence are linked. No unreviewed runtime difference remains.

phases.title: Build, verify and publish the exact image
phases.status: Local image tested; registry publication pending
actions: Prefer promoting the exact tested local image if it matches the accepted runtime source and target architecture. Otherwise build from a clean accepted checkout with VERSION=2.0.0-jq.1, save the source/build metadata, and validate the newly built artifact.

The retained make push-bifrost target tags jq.1 but embeds upstream-only VERSION=2.0.0. Use the explicit full-version build below, or fix and validate that target before relying on it. Verify the API reports v2.0.0-jq.1.

Publish the reviewed artifact as the internal v2.0.0-jq.1 release; record the registry manifest/platform digests and pull it back for verification. A rebuild has its own digest and cannot inherit the old image identity. Pre-pull both old and new artifacts on deployment/recovery hosts and retain the old image.
phases.gate: A registry-pulled image has the expected source, architecture, digest, full API version and passing smoke tests. The deployment can identify it immutably.

phases.title: Prepare deployment and recovery commands
actions: Prepare a reviewed llm-gateway-deploy change for bifrost_image_version: v2.0.0-jq.1 and the recorded immutable artifact. Preserve the installed Portal version, PostgreSQL major version, ingress, encryption configuration and unrelated services. Record resolved digests if the template uses a tag.

Compare the rendered configuration/schema with 2.0, including plugin ordering/PreAuthHook, private plugin URL allowlists, canonical governance routes and pagination, OAuth and cost-breakdown consumers. Preserve all actual Compose overlays, reporting jobs and mounted app data.

Validate the internal entrypoint and inspect its diff. Its execute mode starts eight non-database services together; it does not implement drain → backup → Bifrost-only migration → verify. Prepare and rehearse explicit stage commands or a scoped deployment change that supplies those gates. The ordinary command must not restart stopped writers early.

Prepare full database backup/restore commands, maintenance routing, writer stop/start order and restart controls. Do not combine this upgrade with --update-postgres or Portal --migrate-database unless separately required and rehearsed. Bifrost still migrates its own schema automatically at startup.
phases.gate: An operator has reviewed the exact target paths, Compose project/files, image references, staged cutover commands and complete recovery commands. Configuration diffs contain only intended changes.

phases.title: Rehearse the production-sized upgrade and restore
phases.status: Local functional rehearsal done; production-scale rehearsal pending
actions: Restore a recent full backup in an isolated operator-controlled environment. Prevent accidental production callbacks, jobs or provider traffic; use bounded test keys for intentional live checks. Keep production data and credentials out of the source repository and developer handoff.

Boot the exact old artifact and verify historical records/decryption. Run the proposed migration with the registry artifact and deployment configuration; verify historical and new data, run the smoke matrix, restart 2.0 and confirm migration idempotence.

Restore the full pre-upgrade backup and boot the exact old artifact. Prove old schema, data, decryptability and service behavior return. Measure dump, migration, restore and validation durations at representative size; include resource headroom and a buffer when choosing the window.
phases.gate: The target topology, backup scope, new registry artifact and exact restore procedure pass rehearsal within the agreed outage/recovery budget.

phases.title: Open maintenance and quiesce all writers
actions: Notify users of the maintenance window, stream interruption policy and rollback implications. Freeze configuration changes and deployment automation. Keep health/monitoring access available while inference and management writes are gated.

Drain in-flight requests, long streams and asynchronous uploads/jobs with a recorded timeout. Pause Portal writes, reporting/recalculation jobs and scheduled writers; flush Bifrost logs/object uploads and stop every 1.x Bifrost process.

Prevent supervisors or failover hooks from reviving old instances. Confirm no old sessions or background processes are writing before marking the cutoff time. If traffic cannot drain or a writer cannot be stopped, remain on 1.x and reschedule before migration starts.
phases.gate: All old application writers are stopped, uploads/logs are settled, ingress remains in maintenance and the data cutoff time is recorded.

phases.title: Take and validate the final recovery backup
actions: With writers still stopped, back up every Bifrost config/log database and the full Portal database, including all schema, data and migration state. Capture database roles/grants/extensions needed on the recovery target. Separate database dumps are coherent here because application writes remain quiesced.

Capture configuration/app data and the object-store recovery point as described below. Keep keys available through their existing secure custody. Verify dump completion, archive contents, checksums, backup time and protected off-host copy; do not accept a configuration-only export as rollback coverage.

Validate this final backup by restoring it to a separate recovery target and checking baseline data and old-image access before running the production migration. Include this gate in the window estimate; use a faster tested snapshot/PITR procedure only if it provides the same complete recovery coverage.
phases.gate: The final backup set is complete, coherent, readable and restore-verified; it has an identifier, timestamp, checksums, recovery location and owner.

phases.title: Start one 2.0 instance and let migrations finish
actions: Apply the reviewed Bifrost configuration/image using the staged commands, with public traffic, Portal writers and other jobs still gated. Start exactly one 2.0 Bifrost instance on the intended database and allow its automatic migration to complete.

Watch migration output, database locks, errors, disk growth and memory. Compare migration IDs and schema against the rehearsal; 252 → 290 is the recorded local baseline, not a universal production row-count requirement.

Check readiness and exact version/digest, then restart this instance once under maintenance and verify migration idempotence and historical reads. If migration fails, stop the candidate and use the restore branch below; do not start jq.8 on a partially migrated database.
phases.gate: The expected migration set is present, startup/restart succeeds, no old writer is running, and baseline historical data checks pass.

phases.title: Run the cutover acceptance checks
actions: Run the verification matrix below through the real ingress using an operator-restricted route or test cohort. Resume only the Portal components needed for these checks, with public writes still gated. Use dedicated low-budget keys and record every test write.

Validate historical encrypted data using existing authorized owner/boss key material, plus a new test record. Verify actual production storage mode; if encryption is disabled, retain that mode and use the isolated encryption evidence rather than claiming production ciphertext coverage.

Restart pending admin OAuth flows stored only in old configuration. Verify existing shared/VK credentials and a user OAuth flow. Capture outcomes, timings and request IDs; clean up temporary keys after checks.
phases.gate: Required auth, data, inference, MCP, encryption and billing checks pass; any untested path or known provider limitation is explicitly recorded.

phases.title: Reopen traffic gradually and resume jobs
actions: First reopen to a restricted user/key cohort, then broaden traffic after the agreed observation gate. The single-host environment can gate users at ingress; it does not need a second gateway instance for this step.

Resume Portal writes, reporting and other paused jobs in the rehearsed order. Verify fresh audit records, upload completion, cached-token cost accounting, budgets and dashboard ingestion under real traffic.

For an actual HA environment, update every standby to the verified 2.0 artifact before re-enabling failover. Preserve its single-active Bifrost ownership model; test failover only between upgraded nodes. Never overlap 1.x and 2.0 writers on the migrated schema.
phases.gate: Intended users can use the gateway; all resumed components and any standby run compatible versions, and error/latency/data metrics remain within the agreed thresholds.

phases.title: Observe, reconcile and hand over
actions: Compare success rate, latency, stream endings, log/upload lag, database health, restart count, memory and cost/usage totals with the pre-upgrade baseline. Include one representative reporting/billing cycle before closing the change.

Record final source SHA, registry/platform digests, deploy commit, backup identifier, migration result, test results and start/end times in the release/change record. Keep the rollback owner and recovery materials available during the observation window.

Resume and verify scheduled backups against the 2.0 schema. The existing configuration backup uses an explicit table policy and may reject newly added tables; classify those tables and test backup/restore before relying on it again. Take a new full 2.0 recovery backup.
phases.gate: The observation period and billing/reporting checks pass; 2.0 backups work and the deployment owner accepts the handover.

phases.title: Close the release and retain recovery evidence
actions: Update the release notes, deployment record and this tracker with actual outcomes and any deviations. Keep Bedrock/SGL/Kimi as the agreed pre-existing issues unless their status changes.

Remove temporary test keys and maintenance overrides, restore normal automation, and check that no old instance can restart accidentally. Retain the old image and pre-upgrade backup for the agreed recovery/retention period.

Retire rehearsal resources and expired backups only after the observation and retention gates are met. Store secrets, dumps and recovery private keys under their existing custody rules; commit only sanitized evidence.
phases.gate: Normal operations, monitoring and backups are restored, temporary access is removed, and the release/recovery record is complete.

backups: Full Bifrost configuration and log stores (including separate databases if configured), full Portal data, migration tables, required roles/grants/extensions. For PostgreSQL, use full logical dumps or a tested physical/PITR method; never copy a live PGDATA directory as if it were a consistent backup.

Object payloads and their referenced keys/versions, mounts and file/SQLite stores if present, rendered config/schema, Compose files/overlays and environment configuration. Set a recoverable object-store snapshot/versioning point and pause destructive lifecycle cleanup during the recovery window.

Preserve BIFROST_ENCRYPTION_KEY for stored credentials, existing log owner/boss key material, wrapped-key/passphrase access, OIDC/session secrets, certificates and restore credentials. Keep recovery private keys in their existing separate secure custody; record fingerprints and locations, not secret values.

Exact old/new image digests and source/deploy commits, architecture, database versions/extensions, routing state and external dependencies. Preserve Portal/IdP configuration; back up a locally managed identity store if it is in the change/recovery scope.

A common quiesced cutoff, manifest, checksums, successful separate-target restore and off-host protected copy. Prove both database readability and historical decryption with the old image. Retain monitoring data under its normal backup policy.
upgrade_plan.backup_helper_limit: operations/database/backup-config.sh exports an allowlist of configuration data. Its policy excludes inference logs, MCP logs, temporary OAuth/session data and other runtime records; restore-config.sh restores empty structures for excluded tables. It is useful for configuration recovery but is insufficient for this migration rollback. templates/gateway-ha-backup.sh.j2 is a standby/fault-state hook that stops Bifrost, not a database backup script.
verification: Digest and API version match; migrations complete; restart is idempotent; DB, ingress, monitoring and configured plugins are healthy.

Compare cutoff row counts/IDs and stable payload/cost/usage hashes; verify providers, keys, teams, memberships, routing and aliases. Check actual decrypted OAuth values rather than ciphertext equality when upstream newly encrypts a field.
Portal SSO/admin access; invalid key rejection; team isolation; permitted/denied provider/model paths; low-budget exhaustion; canonical governance APIs and pagination.

Direct OpenAI and OpenRouter via native/integration Responses and streaming/nonstreaming; Codex/Claude MCP continuation; OpenRouter reasoning replay; namespace tool identity; capability rejection and cache_control forwarding. Use existing deterministic evidence for rare stream/SGL/Kimi cases.

Read an old and a new v2 envelope with authorized owner/boss keys; unauthorized access fails. Where S3 offload is configured, confirm object retrieval, correct cached usage and two bounded recalculation passes without object-only payload backfill into SQL. Avoid production-wide recalculation for a smoke test.

New requests produce timely logs/objects, budgets and reports update, no stream stalls or repeated restarts, and latency/error/resource metrics satisfy the recorded thresholds. Remove temporary keys and account for smoke-test spend.
upgrade_plan.coverage_note: Existing local evidence supports these checks; production results must be recorded separately. Bedrock, SGL and Kimi remain accepted pre-existing live-provider limitations. Existing v2 encrypted payloads require no conversion or re-encryption; schema migrations still run. Legacy envelope v1 was not present and is rejected by both current readers.
upgrade_plan.rollback_triggers: Stop progression on a failed/incomplete migration, wrong artifact/version, data loss or decryption failure, authorization regression, repeated crashes, or failure of the working OpenAI/OpenRouter critical paths. For performance, error rate or log lag, use the baseline thresholds and observation duration agreed before the window. If verification cannot finish before the last safe rollback-start time, the deployment owner chooses the pre-agreed restore or extended-outage path.
rollback: If preparation/backup gates fail and the old database has not been changed, restore the old deployment configuration as needed, start the exact old services and reopen after smoke checks. No database restore is needed solely for an aborted pre-migration preparation.

Keep maintenance active and stop all 2.0/application writers. Preserve failure evidence. Restore every database and the matching configuration/object recovery point from the coherent backup; verify all restores succeed before booting the exact old image and Portal configuration. Test old schema/data/decryption, ingress, inference and SSO, then resume traffic and jobs. Account for any test writes discarded by restore.

Drain and stop writes again, record the new cutoff, preserve a full copy of the failed 2.0 state and object references, then restore the old recovery set. Post-backup logs, budgets, users/keys and other changes will be lost from the restored live state. Reconcile them from preserved evidence using a reviewed procedure; there is no verified automatic reverse migration. Do not replay provider calls blindly because they may incur duplicate charges or tool effects.

All stores must reach the same recovery point before any writer restarts. Verify historical content and permissions, exact old artifact, Portal/SSO, inference and reporting. Preserve new-only objects for reconciliation rather than deleting them during rollback. Record actual outage, data-loss interval and recovery results.
upgrade_plan.rollback_limit: A tag change or image-only downgrade is not the rollback procedure. 2.0 merges OAuth tables and drops five old oauth_configs columns. Old and new writers must never share the migrated schema. If zero post-cutover data loss is required, design and rehearse an additional reconciliation strategy before scheduling; the current restore rehearsal does not provide it.

commands.title: Build only, from the clean accepted release checkout
commands.note: This is a proposed build command, not a command executed for this plan. Verify the target architecture and run the new artifact through acceptance before publication. Promoting the already tested image can avoid this rebuild.

commands.title: Deployment preparation for the documented internal environment
commands.code:
# Run in llm-gateway-deploy, on the deployment owner workstation.
./operations/internal/deploy.sh --validate-only
./operations/internal/deploy.sh --check --diff
commands.note: The default config directory is environments/internal. The check connects to deployment hosts; keep generated configuration/diff output private. These checks were not run against production while writing this plan. The execute entrypoint needs the staged cutover handling described in phase 3.

upgrade_plan.ha_note: For a real HA target, the generic deploy.sh uses serial=1 with VIP handoff. That normal rolling path can activate an old standby after another node has migrated the shared schema. Fence old application owners/failover before migration, migrate with one new active instance, upgrade all standbys, and only then restore/test failover. Keep database HA running as appropriate; changing the database topology/version is outside this Bifrost cutover.
